title: Parallel Courses II
summary: Given an integer n representing course labels from 1 to n, and an array relations that specifies prerequisite relationships between courses, where relations[i] = [prevCoursei, nextCoursei] indicates prevCoursei must be taken before nextCoursei, along with an integer k representing the maximum number of courses that can be taken in one semester, determine the minimum number of semesters needed to complete all courses, ensuring all prerequisites are satisfied before a course is taken.
statement: Given an integer n representing course labels from 1 to n, and an array relations that specifies prerequisite relationships between courses, where relations[i] = [prevCoursei, nextCoursei] indicates prevCoursei must be taken before nextCoursei, along with an integer k representing the maximum number of courses that can be taken in one semester, determine the minimum number of semesters needed to complete all courses, ensuring all prerequisites are satisfied before a course is taken.
constraints: Relations form a DAG of prerequisites.
Take at most k currently available courses per semester and minimize semesters.
hints: Encode completed courses as a bit mask.
Derive all unfinished courses whose prerequisite masks are contained in it.
Try every available subset of size at most k and memoize the best remaining semesters.
Every legal semester choice appears once; mask contains all history relevant to future availability.
editorial: Every legal semester choice appears once; mask contains all history relevant to future availability.

tests.explanation: Courses two and three precede one, then course four, requiring three semesters.
Two prerequisite courses can be taken per initial semester, producing four semesters total.
